claims.text: The initial nanoparticles are sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt particles with an FCC crystal structure.
The nanoparticles were synthesized by pulsed laser deposition on a silicon nitride membrane.
The initial nanoparticles have elliptical or icosahedral morphologies.
At elevated temperature, surface-energy-driven segregation kinetically overrides sluggish diffusion in sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Au and Cu have lower surface energies than Co, Ni, and Pt.
Au and Cu migrate to the nanoparticle surface to minimize total free energy.
Segregation produces an Au/Cu-rich surface shell and a Co/Ni/Pt-rich core.
The Au/Cu-rich surface layer evaporates, causing particle mass loss and local compositional change.
Surface segregation and evaporation destabilize the FCC lattice and promote particle coalescence and widening of the size distribution.
For sub-10 nm particles, configurational-entropy stabilization is insufficient to counteract the thermodynamic drive to minimize surface energy.
Increasing temperature overcomes the activation energy for surface diffusion of Au and Cu.
Evaporation-driven compositional change lowers the nanoparticle melting point and accelerates coalescence.
A critical temperature of approximately 850 K ± 50 K marks the onset of dominant Au/Cu segregation and enhanced evaporation.
Above the critical temperature, particles rapidly change from elliptical to spherical shapes and decrease in average size through mass loss.
Surface-energy minimization alone can drive segregation without requiring bulk diffusion barriers to be overcome.
The mechanism applies below 10 nm, where the surface-to-volume ratio is high, and fails above 20 nm, where bulk entropy dominates.
Icosahedral particles segregate faster than truncated-octahedral particles because icosahedral particles have higher surface strain.
High entropy and sluggish diffusion maintain an FCC structure and inhibit segregation up to melting when surface-energy terms are neglected.
The critical temperature can vary with initial stoichiometry, defects, and strain.

contradictions.description: The mechanism requires temperature-activated atomic transport of Au and Cu from the interior toward the surface, but the predicted outcome says surface-energy minimization drives segregation without requiring bulk diffusion barriers to be overcome. These statements need a clearer distinction between surface, subsurface, and bulk diffusion.
